claims.text: Equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi in a simple solid-solution state has low hardness and strength.
The low hardness and strength are governed by a lack of significant lattice distortion.
The low hardness and strength are governed by the absence of precipitation hardening.
The low hardness and strength are governed by the absence of significant solid-solution strengthening.
Controlled heat treatment can introduce an intermetallic or other strengthening secondary phase into CoCrFeNiTi.
Appropriate heat-treatment temperature and duration can promote precipitation while avoiding excessive grain growth or phase segregation.
The heat treatment will form nanoscale precipitates or intermetallic phases within the matrix.
Nanoscale precipitates or intermetallic phases impede dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion increases hardness and strength through precipitation hardening.
Heat-treated CoCrFeNiTi will have significantly higher hardness than the initial simple solid-solution state.
Heat-treated CoCrFeNiTi will have significantly higher strength than the initial simple solid-solution state.
The heat-treated alloy will retain some degree of plasticity.
The proposed mechanism applies to equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi initially in a simple solid-solution state.
The proposed comparison is limited to quasi-static mechanical loading.
The extent of strengthening depends on the heat-treatment parameters and resulting microstructure.
